cues: The dot product proves geometry with almost no effort.
In a parallelogram on a and b, the diagonals are a plus b and a minus b.
Their dot product expands to length a squared minus length b squared.
That is zero exactly when the sides are equal: the diagonals of a parallelogram are perpendicular only in a rhombus.
